pr_title: x86: support single or per-domain page tables
pr_body:
This PR contains many updates towards getting the x86 implementation to match our plans in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/27819. Major updates:

The x86 port used to maintain a separate set of page tables for every user thread. This was ok for 64-bit use-cases where RAM was not much of a concern, but this isn't workable for microcontroller use-cases. This PR implements one of the two page table management schemes described in #27819 
 - By default, page tables are now maintained at the memory domain level, with threads in the same memory domain sharing the same page tables.
 - If `CONFIG_X86_COMMON_PAGE_TABLE` is enabled, there is instead a single set of page tables for all threads/domains that is updated on context switch.
 - For either page table management scheme, x86 allows memory domains to program partitions for any mapped address, not just permanent RAM mappings
 - X86 now implements `struct arch_mem_domain` with page table information if multiple page tables are in use
 - X86 now implements `arch_mem_domain_init()` which creates a fresh set of page tables for the new memory domain, copied from the boot page tables and using the page pool for memory, if we are not using the common page table
 - If multiple page tables are in use, memory mappings are the same across all page tables and all threads. Only permissions with respect to user threads and their memory domain membership is different. Memory access to supervisor mode is the same regardless what thread is scheduled.
 - Since the same page tables could be active on multiple CPUs, implement TLB shootdown logic for SMP.
 - The `z_x86_userspace_enter` implementation now calls back into C code in order to wipe the target stack and update the page table permissions, after switching onto the privilege elevation stack. The US bit for the stack region can only be activated after it has been cleared for security reasons, but before the thread drops privileges.
 - A spinlock now protects the set of active page tables and the slist that links them. All page table modifications are serialized on this lock.
 - We use unused bits in the PTE to backup original page permissions when the mapping was made. This lets us easily restore them when un-applying memory domain partitions.
 - Added build targets to exercise configurations where KPTI is disabled, thanks to @laurenmurphyx64 for the patches
 - Added a test scenario specifically to test memory domain migration, important for SMP if the target thread is running on another CPU.
 - Added qemu_x86_tiny build target, which exercises `CONFIG_X86_COMMON_PAGE_TABLE` with the page pool disabled and a 4MB address space

Fixes: #29175 
Fixes: #29382
Related to: #27819
pr_comments:
Updated PR. Includes test case changes from https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/29461 as the multiple inits of memory domains in that testcase was breaking a lot of stuff.

I believe all the KPTI issues have now been resolved.
tested it on acrn x86 platform, it was fine.

issue_context.title: remove memory domain restriction on system RAM for memory partitions on MMU devices
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
MMU devices have a documented restriction that k_mem_partitions must be within system RAM bounds in order to be programmed into a memory domain.

This is overly restrictive. We should allow k_mem_partition to be installed for any mapped memory address, including virtual mappings from z_mem_map().

The immediate use-case is allowing for user-mode drivers that can be granted access to MMIO regions.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Documentation removed that memory domain partitions can only be SRAM address ranges.
x86 implementation updated to support this.
TBD: can we provide a generic test?
